In March this year, Apple announced the discontinuation of the Mac Pro and confirmed it has no intention of releasing any new Mac Pro hardware.

Bloomberg's latest report today further reveals the full story behind Apple's Mac Pro strategy, including a surprising detail about something Apple was once developing……

The inside story of Apple's shelved Mac Pro plans

In the latest issue of the "Power On" newsletter, Mark Gurman explained that abandoning the Mac Pro "was not always the plan." He reiterated a previously reported key point: Apple originally planned to launch a chip named "Extreme," positioned above the "Ultra" chip.

The report stated: "Apple is said to have developed two chips, the M2 Extreme and M3 Extreme, but ultimately shelved the projects due to considerations of cost and demand."

As for the specific Mac Pro hardware that was in development, Gurman said Apple internally had two models (codenamed J170 and J190) that were never officially released.

The most striking detail in the report is that one of the models used an Intel processor:

Apple officially discontinued the Mac Pro in March, removed it from its official website, and directed buyers to purchase the Mac Studio instead. The ending was actually foreshadowed long ago, but for Mac Pro hardware enthusiasts, it still marks the end of an era, which is inevitably regrettable.

What do you think of Apple's decision to discontinue the entire Mac Pro product line during the Apple Silicon era, rather than continuing to release the "Extreme" chip? Feel free to share your views in the comments section.
